explanation.summary: Connectors are the words that make writing flow. Some join two clauses, and some join two words. They are the difference between a list of sentences and a piece of writing.

sections.heading: Joining clauses
sections.body: Because is porque, although is aunque, so it is por tanto or entonces, and but is pero or sin embargo. The word goes at the start of the second clause, and a comma goes before it. Y is not the equivalent of and: y joins two independent sentences, but for ideas that belong together use sino, but rather.

examples.en: I did not go because I was tired.
I will go, although I do not want to.

examples.es: No es caro; sin embargo, es malo.
examples.en: It is not expensive; however, it is bad.

sections.heading: Joining words and lists
sections.body: To join words use y, o, ni and e. Y becomes e before a word starting with i or hi: innecesario, and Spanish says e in that case. To join a list of more than two, use y before the last one: Madrid, Toledo y Sevilla.

examples.note: E before a word starting with i.

examples.es: Fuimos a Madrid y a Sevilla.
examples.en: We went to Madrid and to Seville.
examples.note: Y before the last item in a list.

examples.en: He speaks neither English nor French.
